cells.tense: You're keeping the thing you built after the ending from being disturbed too soon
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Hand over one finished thing this week and take what comes back for it — once, both directions. Not a keepsake, not a thank-you. Just the exchange.
cells.core:
The clearing has happened and what's left standing is being kept that way — not tying off loose ends, just not disturbing what's settled. You know what's worth holding and what isn't, and you don't announce it. Someone could take the calm for distance. It isn't. Things are still here on purpose, and that's a choice being made daily, mostly without ceremony.

This works through exchange, and holding is where exchange has paused for a while. Let one finished thing leave your hands and take what comes back for it. That's how the stillness stays alive instead of becoming a room nobody's allowed to move in. Some of what you're keeping is ready to be shared and some of it isn't, and you'll know which as you do it.

cells.verb: Holding what the change produced, steady, while it sets

cells.tense: You're bracing for the next ending before the current one has finished settling
cells.act: gather the feelings that might be felt and look at them
cells.ask: Take ten minutes and name what might still be felt about what ended — no decision, no sorting. Just gather it and look at it once.
cells.core:
The clearing worked, and you're guarding the ground it opened so hard that every possible next thing has already been felt in advance. Endings that haven't arrived have been rehearsed. It looks like protecting what you won. From where other people stand, it looks like the ground isn't allowed to just sit.

There's a pile of feeling you haven't looked at directly — not about what ended, about what might. Sit with it ten minutes and decide nothing. Gathering isn't the same as entering. Let the pull stay unclosed, a cloud you're not choosing from yet. When things go well here, you can feel what might come without steeling for it. What you're bracing for gets smaller once it's named in your own voice.

cells.tense: You were standing somewhere else when the ending came, and part of you is still back there
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: The next time something pulls you back toward what ended, name the direction you chose and keep it — once, to yourself, no explanation owed to anyone.
cells.core:
The clearing happened around you and you weren't fully in it. What was supposed to end has ended, and something in you hasn't caught up — still answering an old question, still ready for a room that isn't there anymore. The stillness is real. Your feet aren't quite in it yet.

This works when direction comes from what you actually feel, and the two are out of step for now. What you decided about what comes next is already chosen; keep it past the first tug. Feeling follows movement — it doesn't have to lead it. Say the direction to yourself when the pull comes, and let the rest catch up in time.

cells.tense: You're holding the shape of what came out of the change and calling it just how things are
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: You've already been the one keeping this steady. This week, decide something about it and see it through the same day, without telling anyone.
cells.core:
The shape things are in now was given its shape by someone. You'd say it's how things landed. It landed because you placed it — what stayed, what went, what got kept steady while everything else moved. Your name isn't on that anywhere. The calm holds anyway, and it holds because of the hand you're not mentioning.

What you're maintaining already works; the plainest form of the same move is to decide it, do it, same day, say nothing. No explaining why, no defending the choice. Calling it yours isn't a speech — just the decision, moved through. That's what structure serving what it holds looks like from the inside: quiet, reliable, and yours.

attempts.check: The record does not say what was ended, who left, or how long the clearing took — every cell must stay off that history. A reader could reasonably say nothing was cleared at all, that the stillness is ordinary life and not a harvest; the asks still work as acts performed on what's already here, and the Too Little cell does not need an ending to have happened to use it. The sentence that serves the writer is the one about standing in the doorway; it flatters the pause rather than the person, so it stays out.
